candidates.tagline: Court ordered one sign removed — solution: hide the whole building
candidates.story: A federal court ordered Trump's name removed from the Kennedy Center facade in June 2026; rather than just swap the letters, workers erected a massive tarp covering the entire historic portico — prompting a judge to officially demand an explanation for why a national arts center was under 'marble maintenance.'
candidates.why_funny: The solution to changing one building's lettering was to make the entire building disappear behind a tarp so conspicuous that a federal judge had to write an official order asking why it was there.
candidates.alt: Giant white scaffolding tarp covering the Kennedy Center facade at night, with 'THE JOHN F. K...' letters still visible on the marble to the left, a construction worker in a yellow vest and a truck at lower right

candidates.tagline: Apple's desktop computer: flip it upside-down to turn it on
candidates.story: Apple's M4 Mac mini (launched late 2024) placed the power button on the underside of the device; after 18 months of mockery, Apple 'fixed' this in macOS 26.5 with a Power Control software feature — and the official release notes admit users may 'not have easy access to the computer's power button.'
candidates.why_funny: Apple's answer to 'we put the power button where no one can reach it' was to ship a software update so you can avoid ever touching the power button — rather than move the button.
candidates.alt: Close-up of the dark grey underside of an Apple Mac mini M4, showing the circular ventilation grille and a power button symbol tucked in the corner, photographed from below against a blue background
